chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: In the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام: “If a man is found with a boy in one cover while both are unclothed, the man is to be beaten and the boy disciplined; and if he has penetrated and is muḥṣan, he is to be stoned.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports can bear two interpretations. One of them is that what is intended by them is when the act is short of penetration; then iḥṣān and non-iḥṣān are considered in it. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام explained that in what Sulaymān ibn Hilāl narrated from him, in his saying: “If it is short of penetration, then the hadd is upon him; and if it is penetration, then a blow with the sword.” The doer of that was also called a lūṭī in the narration of Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr which we presented earlier. That does not contradict what we previously presented from Abū Baṣīr from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “That if he penetrates and is muḥṣan, then stoning is upon him.” For when the doer of that has become liable to killing, the Imam may choose between carrying out the hadd on him by striking the neck, casting down from a mountain, burning, or stoning; whichever of these he wills, he may do. Restricting that to his being muḥṣan only indicates, by way of the implication of the wording, that if he is not muḥṣan then that is not upon him; but that may be set aside due to evidence, and we have already presented what indicates that. Nor does that contradict what he narrated:

— (204) 13 — Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd said: I read in the handwriting of a man whom I know, addressed to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and I read the reply of Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in his own handwriting: “Is there a hadd upon a man who played with a boy between his thighs? For some of the group have narrated that there is no harm in a man playing with a boy between his thighs.” So he wrote: “The curse of Allah be upon the one who does that.” This man also wrote, though I did not see the reply: “What is the hadd of two men, one of whom had intercourse with the other willingly between his thighs, and what is his repentance?” So he wrote: “Killing.” “And what is the hadd of two men found sleeping in one garment?” So he عليه السلام wrote: “One hundred lashes.”

Because we interpret this narration as referring to one from whom the act has been repeated, in which case killing becomes obligatory upon him; or we interpret it as referring to one who is muḥṣan. What clarifies what we have mentioned is his statement that upon the two there are one hundred lashes if they are found sleeping in one garment, and we have already explained earlier that this only becomes obligatory with repetition of the act. The other possible approach regarding the reports we presented earlier is that we interpret them as a form of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of some of the ʿāmmah.

key_terms.الإِيقَابِ: penetrative act referred to in the legal distinction discussed in the report
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment, proposed here as an interpretive explanation
key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as one of the punishments mentioned
key_terms.الْإِحْصَانُ: legal state of being muḥṣan, relevant to the ruling mentioned
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the prescribed legal punishment in this context
key_terms.الْقَتْلُ: killing, mentioned as a punishment in certain cases
key_terms.لِحَافٍ: a cover or bedding under which the two were found
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: one possessing iḥṣān, used as a condition in the ruling

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam reconcile different legal reports about liwat and related punishments?
ai.summary: This report presents a legal discussion on rulings related to liwat, citing a narration from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام from the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام and then offering juristic reconciliation between apparently differing reports. It explains possible distinctions between acts involving penetration and those short of it, discusses the role of iḥṣān, repetition of the act, and the possibility that some narrations were issued under taqiyyah.
